problem: is_empty now returns lo >= hi and ignores the closed flags, so closed single points [x,x] are silently dropped when parsing input (:52), intersecting (:92) and building complement gaps (:132, :136); normalize, union, intersection and difference all return wrong results (e.g. difference([(0,2)],[(1,1)]) no longer removes the point 1, intersection([(0,1)],[(1,2)]) returns [] instead of [1,1]).

The change rewrites the emptiness rule that every public operation depends on, but the repository has no tests covering point, half-open-point, touching-intersection or point-subtraction cases, which is how the F1 regression got in unnoticed.
Pre-existing: is_number accepts NaN bounds, so normalize([(nan,1)]) returns [(nan,1,True,True)] and every later comparison, sort and merge on that interval is meaningless.

Pre-existing: validate_bounds accepts a closed explicit infinite bound like (-inf,5,True,True), which export turns into (None,5,True,True), and passing that output back to normalize raises ValueError.
